questions.stem: MRSA is a strain of bacteria resistant to many antibiotics. A hospital prescribes antibiotics to a patient with a bacterial infection. After treatment, most bacteria die but a few resistant ones survive and multiply. Which statement correctly explains why antibiotic resistance develops?

options.text: The antibiotics caused mutations that made the bacteria resistant
The bacteria learned to resist the antibiotic by adapting during their lifetime

Random mutations had already produced resistant individuals before antibiotic use; the antibiotic acted as a selection pressure, killing non-resistant bacteria and allowing resistant ones to survive and reproduce
The patient's immune system made the bacteria stronger

questions.explanation: Antibiotic resistance is a key example of natural selection. Mutations producing resistance arise randomly BEFORE exposure to antibiotics. The antibiotic does not cause the mutation - it acts as a selection pressure. Non-resistant bacteria die, while resistant individuals survive and reproduce, passing the resistance allele to offspring. Over time, the resistant strain becomes dominant.

questions.stem: During the Industrial Revolution, dark-coloured peppered moths became more common in polluted areas while light-coloured moths remained common in clean countryside. Which explanation best applies natural selection to this observation?

options.text: Pollution caused light moths to change colour to dark
Dark moths were camouflaged on soot-covered trees and survived better; light moths were easily spotted by birds and eaten more often
Dark moths migrated to polluted areas because they preferred them
Light moths evolved into dark moths within a single generation

questions.explanation: This is a classic example of natural selection. In polluted areas, tree bark was darkened by soot. Dark moths were camouflaged and less likely to be eaten by birds (the selection pressure), so they survived and reproduced more. Light moths were more visible on dark bark and were eaten more frequently. The allele for dark colouration increased in frequency in polluted populations.

questions.stem: A population of rabbits lives in an area where a new predator is introduced. The predator catches slower rabbits more easily. After many generations, the average running speed of the rabbit population has increased. Put the steps of natural selection in the correct order.

options.text: Predator introduced -> rabbits develop faster legs -> fast rabbits survive
Variation in speed exists -> predator kills slower rabbits -> faster rabbits survive and reproduce -> genes for speed are passed on -> average speed increases over generations
All rabbits run at the same speed -> predator causes mutations -> some rabbits become faster
Fast rabbits are born -> they teach their offspring to run -> the whole population speeds up

questions.explanation: Natural selection follows a clear sequence: (1) variation exists in the population (some rabbits are naturally faster due to genetic differences), (2) a selection pressure acts (the predator catches slower individuals), (3) individuals with advantageous traits survive and reproduce more (differential survival), (4) the beneficial alleles are passed to offspring, (5) over many generations, the frequency of the advantageous allele increases.

questions.stem: Doctors recommend that patients always complete their full course of antibiotics, even if they feel better. How does this advice help prevent the development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria?

options.text: Completing the course prevents the patient from getting the infection again
Completing the course ensures that all bacteria, including those with some resistance, are killed, preventing resistant survivors from reproducing
Stopping early makes the patient's immune system weaker
Completing the course prevents mutations from occurring in the bacteria

questions.explanation: If a patient stops antibiotics early, the least resistant bacteria die first, but bacteria with some resistance may survive. These survivors can then multiply and potentially develop further resistance. Completing the full course maintains antibiotic levels high enough to kill ALL bacteria, including those with partial resistance, preventing them from surviving and passing on resistance genes.

questions.stem: A student says: 'Giraffes evolved long necks because they stretched to reach high leaves.' What is wrong with this statement according to Darwin's theory?

options.text: Giraffes have always had long necks and never evolved

This describes Lamarck's incorrect theory; Darwin's theory states that giraffes with naturally longer necks had a survival advantage and reproduced more, increasing the frequency of long-neck alleles over generations
Giraffes evolved long necks to fight each other, not to reach leaves
The statement is correct according to modern evolutionary theory

questions.explanation: The student is describing Lamarck's disproven theory (inheritance of acquired characteristics). Darwin's theory explains it differently: natural variation meant some giraffes had slightly longer necks due to their genes. These individuals could reach more food, had better survival and reproduction rates, and passed their genes to offspring. Over many generations, average neck length increased through natural selection.
